page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is an x86_64 instance from the High Clock Speed family, powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. The configuration allocates 20 physical cores and 40 virtual CPUs alongside 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.8 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hypervisor operations run on KVM, supported by 35 MB of L3 cache and advanced instruction extensions including AVX-512F and AVX-512 VNNI. The instance features no bundled local storage and no dedicated GPUs, requiring external network-attached volumes over its 12 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark results place the instance consistently within average mid-tier ranges across compute and memory workloads. The system achieves a multi-core Geekbench score of 12,045 and a PassMark CPU rating of 34,691.95, accompanied by 35,214.09 in PassMark extended instruction tests. Memory subsystems deliver 108.89 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 48.09 GB/sec in large-block writes. Key workload metrics reflect 34.78 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks, 25.35 GB/sec in static web serving, and 166.28 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

The absence of local NVMe storage requires architectural consideration for I/O-intensive workloads, redirecting disk operations to network storage over the 12 Gbps interface. Furthermore, CPU-based inference for medium-sized language models remains constrained, delivering 12.71 tokens per second during 7B text generation. Balancing 3.1 GHz dedicated cores with 192 GB of RAM, the instance is well matched for software compilation, caching tiers, backend application hosting, and relational database servers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is a high-clock-speed compute instance featuring 40 vCPUs across 20 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz. It provides 192.0 GB of memory, delivering a balanced 4.8 GB per vCPU ratio, with KVM virtualization and hardware support for AVX-512 and VNNI instruction sets. The server includes no bundled local storage and no GPU accelerators, routing disk traffic and communications through a 12 Gbps baseline network link. Across benchmarks, it sustains mid-tier throughput with a PassMark CPU score of 34,691.95, Geekbench multi-core score of 12,045, and 34.78 million operations per second in Redis SET testing. Without local NVMe disks, persistent storage depends on network attached volumes. This hardware footprint is suitable for enterprise application tiers, in-memory caching platforms, CI/CD build servers, and relational databases.
